'''Mount Aonomine''' (青峰山, Aonomine-san<ref>Mie Prefecture (2005) "[http://www.pref.mie.jp/KAWASABO/HP/kasen/seibi/kamokihon.pdf Basic Policy for River Improvement in the Kamo River System]" p.3</ref>) is a mountain located on the border between {{ill|Toba, Mie|en|Toba, Mie|qid=Q819629|lt=Toba City}} and {{ill|Shima, Mie|en|Shima, Mie|qid=Q338009|lt=Shima City}} in {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en|Mie Prefecture|qid=Q128196|lt=Mie Prefecture}}. It has an elevation of 336 meters.
== Overview ==
Despite its relatively low elevation, Mount Aonomine offers clear views of {{ill|Ise Bay|en|Ise Bay|qid=Q1368308|lt=Ise Bay}}, {{ill|Enshū Sea|en|Enshū Sea|qid=Q11642093|lt=Enshū-nada Sea}}, and {{ill|Kumano Sea|en|Kumano Sea|qid=Q11568930|lt=Kumano-nada Sea}}, making it a landmark for {{ill|kaisen|ja|廻船|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11486879}} sailors in ancient times. The mountain is home to {{ill|Shoufukuji Temple (Toba City)|ja|正福寺 (鳥羽市)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11545590}}, which enshrines a golden statue of {{ill|Kannon|ja|観音}} riding on a {{ill|Whale|ja|鯨|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to クジラ|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q1865281}}. The temple has historically been a site for maritime safety prayers.
The mountain’s forests of {{ill|Castanopsis|en|Castanopsis|qid=Q1065400|lt=Castanopsis}} and {{ill|Cyclobalanopsis|ja|カシ|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q796117}} trees contribute to its scenic beauty, making it a popular spot on the {{ill|Kinki Nature Trail|ja|近畿自然歩道|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11638658}}. While the advent of GPS has reduced its significance as a navigational aid, the area is preserved as a {{ill|Protective Forest for Navigation|ja|航行目標保安林|qid=Q140447333}}. The summit features an observation deck and a digital television relay station, the {{ill|Isobe Relay Station|ja|磯部中継局|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11588064}}.
The haiku pen name of {{ill|Seihō Shimada|ja|嶋田青峰|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11477392}}, a poet from nearby Matoya, is derived from this mountain.<ref>Hosoi (1996): p.48</ref> On May 25, 2016, Canadian Prime Minister {{ill|Justin Trudeau|en|Justin Trudeau}} and his wife {{ill|Sophie Grégoire Trudeau|en|Sophie Grégoire Trudeau}} hiked Mount Aonomine during their visit for the {{ill|42nd G7 Summit|en|第42回先進国首脳会議}} in Ise-Shima.<ref>"Canadian Prime Minister Enjoys Hiking with His Wife on Their Wedding Anniversary," *Chunichi Shimbun*, May 26, 2016</ref> 
== Geography and Geology ==
Mount Aonomine is classified as part of the "Eastern Terrace District," a 100–115 meter hilly region within Toba City.<ref>Toba City History Compilation Office (1991): Upper Volume, p.18</ref> It serves as the source of the {{ill|加茂川|ja|加茂川|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q16279097}}, a secondary river.<ref>Toba City History Compilation Office (1991): Upper Volume, p.20</ref> Geologically, it belongs to the {{ill|Matoya Formation|ja|的矢層群}}, which is part of the {{ill|Shimanto group|ja|四万十層群|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11254492}}, formed during the {{ill|Mesozoic|en|Mesozoic|qid=Q83222|lt=Mesozoic Era}}.<ref>Kawai (1967): p.44</ref>
== Aonomine Trails ==
The mountain has several trails collectively known as "Aonomine Trails":
* '''Matsuo Trail''': Two routes (old and new) starting from Matsuo in Toba City.
* '''Kenko Trail''': A route starting in Kenko in Toba City.
* '''Isobe Trail''': Starting from Izawa-no-Miya Shrine in Shima City.
* '''Matoya Trail''': A drivable route from Matoya Shrine in Shima City.
* '''Gochi Trail''': A pedestrian-only route starting near {{ill|Gochi Station|en|Gochi Station|qid=Q1447309|lt=Gochi Station}} in Shima City.
